title: The neural basis of temporal processing
used_for: Foundational framework: temporal processing is distributed, not centralized; distinguishes dedicated (cerebellum, basal ganglia) vs intrinsic (cortical network dynamics) timing; different timescales use different mechanisms.

title: Distinct Neural Substrates of Duration-Based and Beat-Based Auditory Timing
authors: Teki S, Grube M, Kumar S, Griffiths TD
used_for: fMRI (18 subjects): two distinct timing networks — olivocerebellar (absolute duration) vs striato-thalamo-cortical (beat-based). Accuracy 81.53% irregular vs 84.72% regular; faster RT for regular.

title: Temporal Information Processing in the Cerebellum and Basal Ganglia
authors: Tanaka R, Kameda M, Okada K
journal: Advances in Experimental Medicine and Biology
used_for: Monkey electrophysiology: cerebellum preparatory activity ~500ms pre-movement, subsecond variability regulation; basal ganglia preparatory activity throughout delays up to 2s, duration measurement; fastest rhythmic prediction ~250ms (4Hz).

title: Ramping activity in the striatum
used_for: Computational study: ~1/3 of striatal MSNs show monotonic ramping; emerges at edge of chaos (marginally stable); striatal ramping independent of cortical ramping; up/down ramping populations emerge; D1 vs D2 roles open.

title: Neural population clocks: Encoding time in dynamic patterns of neural activity
used_for: Theoretical review: time encoded in high-dimensional trajectory of population activity; neural sequences vs complex population clocks; striatum higher sequentiality than motor cortex; sequences more flexible than ramping; seconds-to-tens-of-seconds range.

title: Complementary cognitive roles for D2-MSNs and D1-MSNs during interval timing
used_for: Optogenetics + ephys in mice: D2-MSNs increasing, D1-MSNs decreasing across 6s; both accumulate temporal evidence (drift-diffusion R^2=0.95); optogenetic inhibition delays timing (D2 8.6->10.2s p=0.002; D1 8.7->10.5s p=0.03); pharmacological blockade also delays; evidence rated Solid.

title: Modeling Pharmacological Clock and Memory Patterns of Interval Timing in a Striatal Beat-Frequency Model
used_for: SBF model: cortical oscillators (~8-13Hz alpha) -> striatal MSN coincidence detectors; dopamine agonists produce immediate scalar changes in perceived time (clock-speed); model requires biological noise to maintain scalar property; dopamine modulates oscillator frequency, not memory.

title: Time Distortion in Parkinsonism
used_for: Behavioral study in PD: complex timing distortions; motor timing overproduction of short (<2-3s) and underproduction of long (>4s); perceptual rightward bisection shift 2-8s; dopamine binding ratio NOT correlated with timing; challenges simple slowed-clock hypothesis.

title: Taxonomies of Timing: Where Does the Cerebellum Fit In?
used_for: Cerebellum = event-based timing (no beat-based, no continuous); basal ganglia = beat-based; double dissociation (cerebellar patients impaired on single-interval, normal on beat-based); eyeblink conditioning times discrete learned intervals.

title: What makes us tick? Functional and neural mechanisms of interval timing
used_for: Classic pacemaker-accumulator model: pacemaker -> gate switch -> accumulator -> memory -> decision; dopamine controls clock speed (pacemaker rate).

title: What does scalar timing tell us about neural dynamics?
authors: Shouval HZ, Agarwal A, Gavornik JP
used_for: Scalar timing (errors scale linearly with interval) is Weber's law for time; firing rates with log-power form can account for this.
